Use this to fix an entry after you add it, for example a wrong summary, tag, or reference. The CLI has no edit command, so only MCP clients can do this.

## MCP tool

### update_entry

Change fields of an existing entry. Fields that you omit stay as they are.

#### Input

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------------|
| `id` | `string` | yes | Full id or the last 8 characters of the entry. |
| `summary` | `string` | no | One line, max 120 characters. Put longer text in `details`. |
| `details` | `string` | no | New longer text for the entry. |
| `kind` | `"done" \| "blocker" \| "next"` | no | New kind: done, blocker, or next. A change of kind sets the status to open (none for done) and clears the resolution. |
| `project` | `string` | no | New project name. |
| `tags` | `string[]` | no | New tags. They replace the current tags. |
| `refs` | `object[]` | no | New references. They replace the current references. If you also pass `tags`, references that come from ticket-style tags are added to them. |
| `refs.type` | `"pr" \| "jira" \| "commit" \| "url"` | yes | Kind of reference: a PR, a Jira key, a commit, or a URL. |
| `refs.value` | `string` | yes | The PR number, ticket key, commit hash, or URL. |
| `refs.repo` | `string` | no | Repository (owner/name) of the PR or commit. |

#### Output

This tool returns structured output. The shape is the [Entry result](/gournal/docs/reference/output-shapes/#entry-result).
